summary: Mount Hood National Forest lookout site near Sandy, Oregon: an L-5 cab built in 1934 (a 1929 house per the Rex page) half a mile east of the summit, removed in 1967.

facts.design: L-5 cab built about half a mile east of the summit
facts.status_note: Removed in 1967 per the register and the Rex page; firelookout.com says destroyed that year. No source describes standing remains.

staffing.status: emergency lookout in 1938 and listed as one in 1946; last manned year given as 1957 ('probably for the last year')

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mount Hood National Forest)

events.note: Rex page: a lookout house constructed; does not match the register's 1934 cab date
L-5 cab constructed about half a mile east of the summit
Richard Newman appointed emergency lookout for the Walker Prairie station for the fire season (Sandy Post item dated July 27, 1938, quoted on the Rex page)
Entry quoting the Zigzag District's 1957 historical report: manned 'probably for the last year'

July 18, 1959 Oregonian item: city Water Bureau timber sale to clear about 120 acres for a firebreak access road past the station; January 28, 1959 Oregonian item calls the station nearly inaccessible

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex page dates a lookout house to 1929; the register and firelookout.com date an L-5 cab to 1934. The story gives both and does not say whether they are one building.
Register gives 1,900 ft (579 m); firelookout.com gives 2090 ft. Record keeps the register figure; the story gives no elevation.
Record keeps the register point 45.4741, -122.12338; the west_us_lookouts point is about 592 m away. The story gives no coordinates.
Rex page items call the station Walker Prairie while the page itself is titled Walker Peak. The story reports the names as quoted and does not equate them.

corrections.why: No page we read gives a building material for the 1929 house or the 1934 L-5 cab, and the record's design field is null.

notes_for_editor: Kind 'ground' is not stated in any source; the cab is only described as half a mile east of the summit, so kind is left as in the record. The Rex page's 1963 quote on the Walker Point (Western Lane FPA) page names a rebuilt lookout 'Walker Peak Lookout'; see us-or-walker-point-western-lane-fpa. Rex page's 1959 Oregonian and Water Bureau items are quoted second-hand, not read in original.
